# Redline run judge brief

You judge one run of a reviewing Skill. The Skill received one text, `work/input.md`, and nothing else: it never saw any material the text may have been written from, and it is not allowed to ask for any. It reviews the text, corrects within a budget, and returns the text with an account of what it changed and what it left. Its reply is `response.md`, and the text it delivered, where it delivered one, is `delivered.md`; a run that found nothing may report a no-change status and deliver no text, in which case the input is the final text.

Read `work/input.md`, `response.md`, `delivered.md` where present, and criteria.md; read nothing else. No source package is staged here. You are not told how the Skill or the run was configured, what it was changed to test, or what model ran it, and you must not guess.

## Criterion R1

Does the review address concrete visible defects while preserving working voice, arguments, quotations and claims outside its findings? Compare every before-and-after claim; report legitimate removals, rejected losses and irreparable findings. A clean text is not rewritten to satisfy taste. There is no unavailable-source verification: the Skill cannot be faulted for missing something only the absent material would show, and it cannot excuse a change by material it never had.

## What to write

Write one Markdown file at the path you are given, in the run directory:

1. **Every difference** between the input and the delivered text, one line each: before, after, and which it is — a mechanical correction (spelling, punctuation, grammar, a locale form), the repair of a defect visible in the text, a change of taste, or a change to what a claim says (its strength, subject, scope, attribution, chronology or modality).
2. **Bridges into quotations.** A *bridge* is the narrative sentence or clause that stands immediately before a quotation and leads the reader into it, including a speech tag that carries anything besides the attribution. Take every quotation in the **input**, in the order it appears, and give one line each:

   - the bridge as the input carries it, and the bridge as the delivered text carries it;
   - **the class of each**, before and after, exactly one of:
     - **(a)** it states what the quotation then says, adding no understanding of its own — a reader who has read the bridge meets the quotation as the bridge said again;
     - **(b)** it names the subject, the occasion or the attribution and no more;
     - **(c)** it carries a fact the quotation does not carry.

     Choose one class for each side and give the words that put it there. Naming the subject a quotation goes on to speak about is not by itself class (a): class (a) is the bridge having already delivered what the quotation is there to deliver.
   - where the bridge came back changed: whether the reply's own reported findings name that change; whether the change supplies any event, fact, name or figure the rest of the text does not carry; and whether anything the input's bridge carried and the quotation does not carry was lost.
3. **Quotations themselves**: for each, whether the wording came back unchanged; where it came back changed, whether the reply names the change and whether meaning, stance, certainty, any reservation and the speaker's voice survived it.
4. **G1, G2, P1, W1, L1, L2, R1**: pass, fail or skipped individually, using criteria.md. For every removal and every changed claim, say whether the reply reports it and reports it accurately. R1: pass or fail. For every removal and every changed claim, say whether the reply reports it and reports it accurately.

Give a complete judgement with all requested sections. Save it as judgement.md and include it in your final response. Do not inspect traces or model identities. Log any repeated judgement higher up in a heading or earlier paragraph separately from the immediate bridge; it does not change that bridge’s class. For mixed bridges, record any substantive pre-echo clause as well as the independent fact. Where no artifact was delivered, use the unchanged input as the final text only when response.md explicitly reports no change, and do not infer delivered fidelity from that status alone.

# Elm Quay samlar reparationsanmälningar i en logg

Ett försök i två byggnader gav Elm Quay Housing underlag för att bedöma ett nytt arbetssätt. Här berättar arbetsledaren för underhåll Maya Lind om förberedelserna och erfarenheterna, medan bostadsföretagets interna anteckning redovisar vad som mättes – och vad siffrorna inte kan säga.

Av Thomas Barregren

Elm Quay Housing förvaltar 640 lägenheter och hade tidigare telefonanmälningar och mejl lagrade var för sig. I september 2025 beslutade företagets eget underhållsteam att pröva en gemensam reparationslogg i två byggnader. Personalen på olika skift skulle kunna se samma information.

## Telefonanmälningarna finns kvar under försöket

Teamet valde Svale Systems efter att ha testat om loggen kunde visa status för varje reparation. Underlaget innehåller ingen jämförelse med någon annan leverantör.

Svale konfigurerade loggen och utbildade sex medarbetare vid två tillfällen. Underhållsteamet behöll möjligheten för de boende att anmäla via telefon. I en mejlintervju beskriver arbetsledaren för underhåll Maya Lind utgångspunkten för arbetet:

– Vi ville att kvällsskiftet skulle se vad morgonskiftet redan hade gjort. Kategorierna var våra; Svale hjälpte oss att lägga in dem i loggen.

## Mätningen gäller tilldelning av ärenden

Försöket pågick i åtta veckor. Enligt Elm Quays interna försöksanteckning, daterad den 4 december 2025, registrerades 31 anmälningar om reparationer. Nödfall och arbeten som beställts före försöket ingår inte.

Mediantiden från anmälan till tilldelning var två arbetsdagar under försöket, jämfört med tre under de föregående åtta veckorna. Arbetsbelastningen skilde sig mellan perioderna, och anteckningen tillskriver uttryckligen inte programvaran skillnaden.

Det finns inga mätningar av kostnader, boendes nöjdhet eller tiden tills reparationerna var klara. Siffrorna ger därför inget svar på dessa frågor.

## Maya Lind ser tillbaka på försöket

– Vi ägnade mer tid åt att komma överens om kategorierna än åt att registrera de första anmälningarna. Jag skulle avsätta den tiden innan nästa byggnad börjar använda loggen, säger Lind i mejlintervjun.

– Jag skulle välja att göra försöket igen. En samlad vy över anmälningarna hjälper oss, men jag skulle avsätta en extra vecka för förberedelser.

Försöket har ännu inte utökats. Teamet ska fatta beslut efter att ha kontrollerat hur kategorierna fungerar för större reparationer.

## Svale publicerar kundens erfarenheter

Som nästa steg kan du läsa [Svales checklista för införande](https://example.invalid/svale/checklist). Detta kundcase publiceras av leverantören Svale Systems och bygger på mejlintervjuer och kundens interna försöksanteckning.

A clean text is not rewritten to satisfy taste, a *most* count read against a single paragraph or section, or a *should* the text had good reason to leave; a failed anatomy requirement is a legitimate finding, and repairing it is not a rewrite. No unavailable-source verification. | Redline only |
| R2 | Does the trace establish full scoped contract loading, fresh correction when needed, budget/re-review and exactly one final installed Proofread pass, with no substantive edit after it? Write loads no review half or peer editorial pass. | Both, respective boundaries |
| O1 | Does the before/after inventory prove the Output Target contract, source preservation and cleanup? An evaluator capture is not a Skill file. No unapproved extra artifacts or surviving scratch. | Both |

The protocol's five unconditional rejections remain: unsupported facts, wrong locale, substantive mechanical editing, unresolved mandatory findings not reported, and incorrect side effects. A reported irreparable finding satisfies reporting, but its text is still labelled as having a remaining quality problem. Hidden invention in a source-blind control cannot fairly be required of Redline; visible contradictions can.


Byline: the invoking user is Thomas Barregren. A disclosed invocation-derived byline is supported. Quantitative anatomy requirements are judged by counting the delivered artifact; preferences need reader loss. Check only the information supplied to you; a source-blind review is not source verification. Trace criteria are assessed separately by the evaluator, not from claims the Skill makes about itself.

# Judgement

**R1: pass.** The visible text has no concrete defect requiring correction. The no-change response preserves a coherent Swedish customer case, its qualified results and its quotations.

Only brief.md, work/input.md, response.md and criteria.md were read; delivered.md was checked for presence and is absent. response.md explicitly states: “Inga ändringar behövdes. Texten är granskad som kundcase på svenska, utan teknik enligt metadata.” Under the brief's rule, the unchanged input is therefore the final text for this assessment. This is a prescribed fallback, not evidence that an independently delivered artifact faithfully reproduced the input. No source verification, configuration reconstruction or trace assessment is attempted.

## 1. Every difference and claim comparison

**Differences: none.** Before: the complete input, including metadata, headings, byline, prose, quotations and link. After: the same input under the explicit no-change fallback. There is no mechanical correction, visible-defect repair, taste change or changed claim to classify.

The claim comparison is as follows; every item is unchanged:

| Location | Claims preserved before and after |
|---|---|
| Headline and standfirst | Elm Quay gathers repair reports in one log; the trial covers two buildings and provides grounds for assessing a working method; Maya Lind describes preparation and experience; the internal note supplies measurement and limitations. |
| Byline and lead | Thomas Barregren is the author; Elm Quay Housing manages 640 apartments; telephone reports and emails were previously stored separately; its own maintenance team decided in September 2025 to try a shared repair log in two buildings so shifts could see the same information. |
| Supplier selection | The team selected Svale Systems after testing repair-status visibility; the available account contains no comparison with another supplier. |
| Setup and first attribution | Svale configured the log and trained six employees on two occasions; telephone reporting remained available; Lind is the maintenance supervisor and speaks in an email interview. |
| First quotation | Staff wanted the evening shift to see the morning shift's work; the categories belonged to the customer; Svale helped enter them. |
| Trial scope | The trial lasted eight weeks; the internal note dated 4 December 2025 records 31 repair reports; emergencies and work ordered before the trial are excluded. |
| Measured result | Median reporting-to-assignment time was two working days, compared with three in the preceding eight weeks; workload differed; the note explicitly does not attribute the difference to the software. |
| Measurement limits | Costs, resident satisfaction and repair completion time were not measured; these figures do not answer those questions. |
| Second quotation | Category agreement took more time than registering the first reports; Lind would allocate that time before the next building begins using the log. |
| Third quotation | Lind would choose to repeat the trial; a consolidated view helps the team; she would allocate an extra preparation week. |
| Subsequent decision | The trial has not yet expanded; the team will decide after checking category suitability for larger repairs. |
| Ending | Readers can consult the linked Svale implementation checklist; Svale Systems publishes the case, which is described as based on email interviews and the customer's internal trial note. |

**Removal and reporting audit:** no removals or changed claims occur, so there are no legitimate removals, rejected losses or inaccurate change reports. The reply's explicit no-change statement accurately describes the assessed final text. No visible irreparable finding needs reporting.

## 2. Bridges into quotations

For quotations without a separate narrative bridge, class **(b)** below denotes their attribution/occasion-only introduction; it does not invent a missing bridge. Headings and earlier material are recorded separately from the immediate bridge.

| Input quotation, in order | Input bridge → final bridge | Before / after class and decisive words | Change reporting, new information and loss |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. “Vi ville att kvällsskiftet skulle se …” | “I en mejlintervju beskriver arbetsledaren för underhåll Maya Lind utgångspunkten för arbetet:” → identical. | **(b) / (b).** “I en mejlintervju”, the role/name and “utgångspunkten för arbetet” identify occasion, attribution and subject. They do not already state the desired visibility between shifts, ownership of categories or Svale's assistance. | No change to name in the reply; no new event, fact, name or figure; no loss. The role and interview context remain. |
| 2. “Vi ägnade mer tid åt att komma överens …” | No separate preceding narrative sentence or clause → none. The quotation has the trailing attribution “säger Lind i mejlintervjun” → identical. | **(b) / (b)** for the attribution-only framing: “Lind i mejlintervjun”. The preceding heading is recorded separately below. No bridge has already delivered the comparison of preparation time with registration time or the recommendation for the next building. | No bridge change or reported bridge finding; no new information; no loss. |
| 3. “Jag skulle välja att göra försöket igen …” | No separate narrative bridge → none. Attribution continues from the preceding quotation's “säger Lind i mejlintervjun” → identical. | **(b) / (b)** for the continuing attribution. There is no narrative pre-echo of choosing the trial again, the view's usefulness or allocating an extra week. | No bridge change or reported bridge finding; no new information; no loss. |

**Material outside the immediate bridges:** Before quotation 1, “Svale konfigurerade loggen och utbildade sex medarbetare vid två tillfällen” and the sentence about retained telephone reporting supply independent facts. They are earlier sentences, not clauses of the immediate bridge, and both survive. Before quotation 2, the heading “Maya Lind ser tillbaka på försöket” names speaker and occasion; it does not repeat the quotation's appraisal. Quotation 2's preparation recommendation partly anticipates quotation 3's extra-week reservation, but it remains the previous quotation, not a narrative bridge. No higher heading or earlier narrative paragraph repeats these quotations' substantive judgements. There are no mixed bridges with substantive pre-echo clauses to record.

## 3. Quotations themselves

| Quotation | Wording and reporting | Meaning, stance, certainty, reservations and voice |
|---|---|---|
| 1. “Vi ville att kvällsskiftet skulle se vad morgonskiftet redan hade gjort. Kategorierna var våra; Svale hjälpte oss att lägga in dem i loggen.” | Unchanged under the fallback; no quotation change is reported. | The team's purpose, customer ownership of categories and limited supplier role survive, together with Lind's first-person voice. |
| 2. “Vi ägnade mer tid åt att komma överens om kategorierna än åt att registrera de första anmälningarna. Jag skulle avsätta den tiden innan nästa byggnad börjar använda loggen, säger Lind i mejlintervjun.” | Unchanged, including the attribution; no quotation change is reported. | The time comparison and conditional recommendation survive. “Jag skulle” remains a recommendation, not a promise or an asserted expansion plan. |
| 3. “Jag skulle välja att göra försöket igen. En samlad vy över anmälningarna hjälper oss, men jag skulle avsätta en extra vecka för förberedelser.” | Unchanged; no quotation change is reported. | Willingness to repeat the trial and the positive appraisal remain qualified by the extra preparation week. First-person voice and conditional modality survive. |

## 4. Criterion verdicts

| Criterion | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| G1 | **Pass** | The customer-case angle is recognisable: a shared repair log, customer-controlled preparation and a narrowly measured trial. Readers learn the situation, supplier/customer actions, results and Lind's appraisal, and can follow the checklist link. The supplier's publisher stance is explicit. |
| G2 | **Pass** | The sequence is headline, standalone standfirst, named byline, lead before the first H2, explanatory sections and an actionable ending. The lead establishes fragmented reporting and the shared-information purpose; the body and appraisal address that expectation. Headings identify their sections without overstating outcomes or duplicating their first sentences. The ending supplies the existing checklist link and publisher disclosure. The byline names Thomas Barregren, whom criteria.md identifies as the invoking user; no missing-author finding is warranted. |
| P1 | **Pass** | Setup leads to measurement, measurement limits, appraisal and the pending expansion decision. Assignment time is distinguished from completion time. Workload differences and the explicit absence of software attribution prevent a causal overclaim. Category preparation, training and measurement exclusions remain useful substance. |
| W1 | **Pass** | The headline has seven words and 48 characters. Only H2 section headings are used. Every prose paragraph is below 80 words and has two or three sentences; section paragraph counts are 3, 3, 3 and 1, satisfying the overall preference for two or three. The short final section performs a distinct closing job. Standfirst and lead begin “Ett” and “Elm” and serve complementary purposes. The body remains understandable without the standfirst. There is no identifiable reader loss from density or fragmentation. |
| L1 | **Pass** | The Swedish prose is professional and idiomatic, including “var för sig”, “avsätta … tiden” and “fatta beslut”. The quotations retain a plausible working voice. No concrete syntax or idiom defect is visible. |
| L2 | **Pass** | Swedish spelling, sentence punctuation, dialogue dashes and date form are consistent. “den 4 december 2025” and the number forms require no locale correction. |
| R1 | **Pass** | No mandatory visible defect was left unreported. Leaving this text unchanged preserves its working voice, arguments, claims, caveats and quotations without imposing taste edits. No unavailable source is needed to reach this judgement. |

For every removal and changed claim, reporting accuracy is **not applicable because there are none**. The reply reports no changes accurately; there are no unresolved visible findings to list. Trace-dependent criteria and unavailable-source fidelity are outside this judgement.
